validity.researcher_notes: Flag: Status=operating but StartYear1 blank. Independent research: this row (750 MMcf/d capacity, Al Gamil/Port Said to Damietta, Owner split Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co 48% / Eni 26% / Naturgy 13% / SEGAS 13%) matches EXACTLY the pipeline described in Al Borsa (alborsaanews.com, 2019-03-17): a dedicated land connector Eni built from the Zohr gas-treatment plant at El Gamil (Port Said) to the Damietta liquefaction (SEGAS/Damietta LNG) plant, sized at 750 MMcf/d, with that same 48/26/13/13% ownership split — built specifically so Eni could export its Zohr equity gas via Damietta LNG. That article (published March 2019) reported the physical pipeline would finish 'next April' (April 2019); Daily News Egypt (2020-03-03) independently reported the land pipeline as already 'completed' by that point, but Eni was still only 'seeking' to start exporting gas through it that year (2020) — i.e. gas had not yet begun flowing through the connector for its intended purpose as of March 2020. The reason: Damietta LNG plant itself had been idle since Nov 2012 and did not resume operations until the Naturgy/Eni/EGAS/EGPC settlement closed and the plant produced and lifted its first LNG cargo since 2012 on 22–23 Feb 2021 (Eni press release; LNG Industry; Enerdata — three independently-run outlets all confirming the same Feb 2021 restart, explicitly tied to Zohr/Eni gas availability). Since this specific connector's sole documented purpose is feeding Eni's Zohr-equity gas to Damietta LNG for export, and there is no evidence it carried material volumes for any other purpose in 2019–2020, the best-supported 'start of operation' year for the pipeline is 2021 (when its destination plant actually began receiving/exporting gas), not 2019 (when the pipe was merely reported physically complete). No source explicitly states 'the Al Gamil–Damietta pipeline began carrying gas on this exact date' — the 2021 date is the most defensible inference chain from independently-sourced facts, not a guess, and is flagged medium rather than high for that reason. Considered but rejected: egy-map.com (an Egyptian project-tracker page) gives a conflicting 'May 2018' completion date and describes a broader domestic-supply function (feeding Al-Burullus power station, serving Damietta/Port Said governorates generally) with no mention of Zohr or Eni — this reads as a different/generic project description, not a match to this row's specific 750 MMcf/d Zohr-export spec, so it was not used as evidence.

fills.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2021: the year Damietta LNG (this connector's sole documented destination/purpose, per Al Borsa's matching 750 MMcf/d Zohr-export spec) actually began receiving/exporting gas after its 2012–2021 idle period, per Eni's own restart announcement (first cargo lifted 22 Feb 2021) and two independent trade-press confirmations (LNG Industry, Enerdata). The physical pipe was reported complete by ~April 2019 (Al Borsa) but not yet carrying its intended export volumes as of March 2020 (Daily News Egypt), so 2019 was rejected as the operational start year in favor of 2021. Flagged medium tier: the 2021 date is a well-sourced inference tying this row to the Damietta restart, not a source naming this pipeline's exact commissioning date directly — recommend Baird spot-check against Eni's Egypt asset filings or an EGAS annual report if a firmer date is wanted.
